title: Tabular Data Type
description: Tabular data type aligned with CDIF 2026 schema using DDI-CDI and CSVW properties. Typed as cdi:TabularTextDataSet and ada:tabularData.

ada:componentType.description: ADA componentType for a tabular data file, as a single string. Allowed values are constrained at the technique-profile level.

ada:xCoordCol.description: The column names are redundant, they are lists in the hasPhysicalMapping array. Include here for convenience.

ada:spatialRegistration.title: Spatial Registration Type
ada:spatialRegistration.description:
The affine transform from an image's pixel coordinates to a coordinate reference system defined on the sample -- origin, pixel scales, rotation and axis sense -- for spatially registered images and maps.
MODELLED ON A WORLD FILE, the sidecar a GIS writes beside a raster (.tfw, ESRI .wld), whose six parameters are exactly an affine transform. In world-file letters:

    x_crs = ada:originX + ada:pixelScaleX * col + ada:pixelRotationX * row     (C, A, B)
    y_crs = ada:originY + ada:pixelRotationY * col + ada:pixelScaleY * row     (F, D, E)

DEPARTURES FROM THE WORLD-FILE CONVENTION. Three, each of which says more rather than less -- and each of which a converter has to handle deliberately, because none is a straight copy:

  1. ORIGIN CORNER IS DECLARED, NOT ASSUMED. A world file assumes C,F is the centre of the
     upper-left pixel. Here ada:originLocation states the corner (upperLeft, upperRight,
     lowerLeft, lowerRight, center) and ada:coordDef states what the coordinates are measured
     from. Reading a .tfw therefore means WRITING originLocation: upperLeft explicitly; it is
     not implied.

  2. ada:pixelScaleY IS A MAGNITUDE, NOT A SIGNED VALUE. A world file conventionally makes E
     negative to encode the y-axis flip. Here the axis sense is carried by ada:originLocation,
     so the sign is NOT part of the scale. Importing E means taking its absolute value and
     recording the flip as a corner; exporting means re-applying the sign. Copying E straight
     into ada:pixelScaleY silently halves nothing and mirrors everything.

  3. UNITS ARE CARRIED, WHERE A WORLD FILE HAS NONE. ada:pixelUnits and ada:coordUnits state
     both sides of the scale. A world file is unitless and takes its units from the raster CRS,
     so an import has to source them from elsewhere and cannot leave them absent -- which is
     why ada:pixelUnits is in the inline required list.

SCALING AND REGISTRATION ARE SEPARABLE, and $defs/Scaling below is the half that is meaningful on an UNREGISTERED image: a plain ada:image has a pixel size, and ada:pixelScaleX on an ada:EPMAImage is a well-formed statement. Registration is the other half -- where the image sits on the sample, and how its axes relate to the sample's -- and only a map can assert it. The root schema here is scaling PLUS registration and is what the imageMap block references; the image block references $defs/Scaling. One property name, two shapes, so a placement path through either branch resolves.

allOf.title: Pixel Scaling
allOf.description: Pixel size and its units: the half of a spatial registration an UNREGISTERED image can state. Nothing is required, because an image may know its scale or not, and demanding one would make the property unusable on the images that do not -- which is exactly why the image block carried no spatialRegistration at all before this split, the only available shape having required an origin, a corner and a coordinate definition.

ada:pixelUnits.description: Units of ada:pixelScaleX/Y, e.g. nm, um, mm. Normalise before comparing values.

ada:pixelScaleX.description: CRS units per column step (world-file A).

ada:pixelScaleY.description: CRS units per row step (world-file E). A world file conventionally makes this NEGATIVE to encode the y-axis flip; here the sense is carried by ada:originLocation, so this is a magnitude.

ada:basemap.description: link to appropriate basemap image map

ada:originX.description: CRS x of the origin pixel (world-file C). Which pixel that is, is stated by ada:originLocation rather than assumed to be the upper-left.

ada:originY.description: CRS y of the origin pixel (world-file F).

ada:originZ.description: CRS z of the origin pixel, where the registration is to a three-dimensional frame. A world file has no equivalent, and a planar thin section does not need one.

ada:coordDef.description: Whether coordinates are stage-defined or pixel-defined. If pixel-defined, are coordinates from stage, upperleftPixel, or centerPixel.

ada:coordUnits.description: Units of the CRS coordinates, i.e. of originX/Y/Z. A world file carries no units.

ada:pixelRotationX.description: The x-component of one ROW step (world-file B): how far CRS x moves per row, which is zero when the image axes are parallel to the sample axes. Non-zero whenever the stage was rotated relative to the sample frame -- the case a scale-and-origin model cannot express at all, which is why both off-diagonal terms are declared here rather than assumed away.

ada:pixelRotationY.description: The y-component of one COLUMN step (world-file D): how far CRS y moves per column, zero for an axis-aligned image. Optional, and absent means zero, so a registration that omits both rotation terms is the axis-aligned case -- which is what every record carries today.

ada:originLocation.description: The location of the origin pixel of an image. Range: upperLeft, upperRight, lowerLeft, lowerRight, center

ada:worldFile.description:
Link to an EXTERNAL world file that carries the affine transform, instead of stating the six parameters inline -- a .tfw beside a GeoTIFF, an ESRI .wld, or any sidecar of that form. Use it when the transform already exists as a file the instrument or the processing software wrote: restating those numbers by hand is a second copy that can disagree with the first, and the file is the authority.
A record states the transform ONE way or the other, which the anyOf below enforces: either the inline parameters (origin, scales, corner, coordinate definition) or this reference. Both together is permitted and is not recommended -- nothing can adjudicate a disagreement between them, and the inline copy is the one that goes stale.
READ THE DEPARTURES BELOW BEFORE TRUSTING A ROUND TRIP. A world file is not quite what this object says, so importing one into the inline terms, or writing one out from them, needs the sign and the unit handled deliberately rather than copied.

anyOf.title: Reference to an external world file

allOf.title: Tabular Data Type
allOf.description: Tabular data type aligned with CDIF 2026 schema using DDI-CDI and CSVW properties. Typed as cdi:TabularTextDataSet.

cdi:commentPrefix.description: Character(s) that mark a line as a comment.

cdi:isDelimited.description: Schema constraint is that one of {'isDelimited','isFixedWidth'} must be present with a True value; the other one may be present or omitted, but if present must have a false value.

cdi:lineTerminator.description: Allowed line terminators, in order (default [CRLF, LF]).

cdi:escapeCharacter.description: The character used to escape special characters in the data. From DDI-CDI PhysicalSegmentLayout.escapeCharacter.

cdi:headerIsCaseSensitive.description: Whether column header names are case-sensitive. From DDI-CDI PhysicalSegmentLayout.headerIsCaseSensitive.

cdi:treatConsecutiveDelimitersAsOne.description: Whether consecutive delimiters should be treated as a single delimiter. From DDI-CDI PhysicalSegmentLayout.treatConsecutiveDelimitersAsOne.

cdi:tableDirection.description: Direction in which columns are arranged in each row (DDI-CDI TabularTextDataSet.tableDirection, TableDirectionValues enumeration).

cdi:textDirection.description: Reading order of text within cells (DDI-CDI TabularTextDataSet.textDirection, TextDirectionValues enumeration).

cdi:trim.description: Which spaces to remove from a data value (DDI-CDI TabularTextDataSet.trim, TrimValues enumeration).

cdif:hasPhysicalMapping.description: Links variables to their physical representation in this dataset.

items.title: Physical Mapping Type
items.description: Defines implementation-specific properties for the representation of a variable in a dataset. Aligned with CDIF 2026 schema using DDI-CDI flat per-column mapping structure.

@type.description: Must include a physical-mapping family type. A plain physical mapping uses cdif:PhysicalMapping; the cdifTextMapping / cdifLocatorMapping specializations narrow this to cdif:TextMapping / cdif:LocatorMapping respectively (they compose this schema via allOf, so the base accepts any of the family rather than requiring the cdif:PhysicalMapping token).

cdif:index.description: Non-negative integer that orders the fields in the data structure (column number).

cdif:format.description: A format for number expressed as a string, or date format like YYYY/MM or MM-DD-YY.

cdif:physicalDataType.title: CDIF Concept-or-Term-or-String
cdif:physicalDataType.description: identifier or name for the data type concept.

anyOf.description: A SKOS concept identified by URI, a schema:DefinedTerm, or an inline cdif:Concept. Shared shape used wherever a CDIF property carries either a controlled-vocabulary reference or an inline concept definition.

@id.description: reference to a skos concept for the data type

anyOf.description:
schema.org Defined Term schema.

**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:DefinedTerm is represented by a single attribute of that class type.
The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value to be EITHER a
plain string (interpreted as schema:name or schema:termCode in the default
vocabulary) OR a full schema:DefinedTerm object (with explicit @type, name,
identifier, termCode, inDefinedTermSet). Consumers should accept either form.

Note that this differs from the cdif Concept policy: a Concept (skos:Concept)
in CDIF profiles MUST be a controlled-vocabulary entry (object form or
@id-reference) — plain strings are not permitted for Concept-typed values
because vocabulary identity cannot be recovered from an unscoped label.

schema:name.description: text label for the term that is useful to human user

anyOf.description:
Properties for a schema.org identifier (schema:PropertyValue pattern).
**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:Identifier / schema:PropertyValue is represented by a single attribute
of that class type. The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value
to be EITHER a plain string (interpreted as the bare identifier value) OR a
full schema:PropertyValue object (with explicit @type, propertyID, value).
Consumers should accept either form.

schema:propertyID.description: In this context for the schema:PropertyValue, this field is an identifier for the identifier schema, e.g. DOI, ARK.  Get values from https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ for interoperability. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}) so they participate in RDF entailment; free-label strings remain valid as strings.

schema:url.description: web-resolveable string for the identifier; host name part is location of a resolver that will return some representation for the given identifier value. E.g. https://doi.org/10.5066/F7VX0DMQ

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description: The controlled vocabulary responsible for this keyword, as EITHER a plain URI string identifying the vocabulary, OR an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere in the document. Both forms are already in use across CDIF profiles and downstream ADA building blocks; permitting only the string form made the object form - the natural JSON-LD spelling of a reference - invalid, while this class's own union-type policy above explicitly anticipates both.

schema:termCode.description: A representative code for this keyword in the controlled vocabulary. Analogous to skos:Notation

cdi:numberPattern.description: Number format pattern for the field (PhysicalMapping.numberPattern). Text-format properties (column width, decimal/digit-group separators, display label) live on cdifTextMapping.

cdi:nullSequence.description: The value of this property becomes the null annotation for the described column.

cdi:defaultValue.description: A default string indicating the value to substitute for an empty string.

cdif:formats_InstanceVariable.description: Reference to a variable defined in schema:variableMeasured.

@id.description: This should be a reference to a variable defined in the schema:variableMeasured section.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Soft-typed extension properties. The row and column counts live here rather than as bare properties, so that each carries a schema:propertyID identifying the concept it quantifies - DDI Discovery caseQuantity for the row count and variableQuantity for the column count. As bare unprefixed `countRows`/`countColumns` they were the only two properties on this class with no namespace and no definition, so nothing said what they meant or tied them to a vocabulary.

items.title: additionalProperty PropertyValue
items.description: PropertyValue values required to define a soft-typed property with a value.

@context.description: JSON-LD context declaring the skos namespace prefix. May be a single object or an array of strings and objects.

skos:prefLabel.description: Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string, a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values. Each language should appear at most once.

skos:notation.description: Classification code for this concept within a scheme (a single notation string, consistent with CdifCodelistConcept).

skos:definition.description: Formal explanation of the meaning of this concept.

skos:scopeNote.description: Note clarifying meaning and/or intended use.

skos:historyNote.description: Note about past state or use.

skos:inScheme.description: Concept scheme(s) this concept belongs to.

skos:topConceptOf.description: Concept scheme(s) for which this is a top concept.

skos:broader.description: Broader (parent) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

anyOf.description: A reference to a SKOS Concept by URI.

skos:narrower.description: Narrower (child) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

anyOf.description: A reference to a SKOS Concept by URI.

LanguageTaggedValue.description: An RDF literal value with a language tag, serialized as a JSON-LD value object.

@language.description: BCP 47 language tag (e.g. en, fr, de).
